content:
Requirement R17 (input): Command Track Target of Interest (TOI). Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to command tracking of a target of interest..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-17.1, F-17.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-17.<F>.1, Be-17.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-17.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** Let the pilot designate a target of interest and command the UAV to track (center ISR sensors on) it.

**Function candidates:**

**F-17.1 — Target designation-to-track function.** The HMI's purpose is to convert a pilot-identified target into a validated tracking command sent to the UAV. Goal: turn "that thing there" into an actionable, confirmed track order. Measurable by designation accuracy and command-completion rate.

**F-17.2 — Track-execution confirmation function.** The HMI's purpose is to confirm to the pilot that the UAV has accepted and is executing the track (sensor centered on TOI). Goal: close the loop so the pilot knows tracking is live. This is the return-path teleology (steps 7.1.7–7.1.10), distinct from issuing the command.

**F-17.3 — Track-order tasking reception function.** The HMI's purpose is to make an incoming target-tracking *order* (7.1.1) known to the pilot before they act. Goal: pilot awareness of the tasking.

Note: **F-17.3 overlaps heavily with R06/R08** (order communication + notification framework) — I'd flag it as already-covered rather than redesign it here. **F-17.2** overlaps with the R02/R08 acknowledgment pattern reused across R10–R13. So the genuinely *new* teleology for R17 is **F-17.1** — the designation-to-track command itself.

Recommendation: close on **F-17.1**. Which do you want?

**F-17.1 — Target designation-to-track function** is closed.

Moving to Behaviour. One pathway per fixed modality (Touch, Keyboard), plus Mixed if it adds value.

**Be-17.1.1 — Touch-only.** Pilot taps the TOI directly on the map/sensor-feed (or the TDC cursor rate-points to it), producing a designation marker. A confirm-gated TRACK action (touch CONFIRM) validates the designation is a trackable target and issues the command. Full task completable by touch alone.

**Be-17.1.2 — Keyboard-only.** Pilot enters/selects the target by identifier or coordinates via UCP alphanumeric + bezel OSS stepping through a candidate/target list, then bezel CONFIRM issues the track command. No pointing device required — usable when hands-off-throttle pointing isn't viable or when the TOI is a known catalogued contact.

**Be-17.1.3 — Mixed.** Touch/TDC designates the point on the map, keyboard/OSS refines or overrides (e.g. snap to a listed contact, adjust the designation) and confirms. Adds value: spatial pick is fastest for "that one," while keyboard disambiguates when multiple contacts cluster near the tap.

The confirm-gate itself is the **reused dual-input CONFIRM pattern** (R09/R10 lineage) — flag: shared, not new to R17. The designation-marker map interaction is close to **R14's sensor aim-point designation** (map-tap/drag with confirm-gated slew) — R17 designates a *target to track* rather than a *sensor aim-point*, but the interaction primitive is the same. Worth reusing R14's designation mechanism rather than inventing a parallel one.

Recommendation: keep all three; Mixed (Be-17.1.3) is the primary pathway since target clusters are the realistic ISR case. Agree?

All three behaviours retained: **Be-17.1.1 (Touch-only)**, **Be-17.1.2 (Keyboard-only)**, **Be-17.1.3 (Mixed)**.

Moving to Structure. Concrete HMI element sets implementing these pathways.

**S-17.1.1 — Map/feed designation + reused confirm gate (serves Be-17.1.1, Be-17.1.3).**
- Reuse **R14's designation mechanism** on the Map view / ISR MONITOR pane (R16): touch-tap or TDC rate-cursor drops a TOI marker; distinct marker style from R14's sensor aim-point (target reticle vs. aim crosshair) so the two designations don't collide visually on the same map.
- **TRACK TOI** action button (WAD on-screen + bezel OSS mirror) → reused **dual-input press-and-confirm gate** (R09/R10 lineage).
- Envelope/trackability validation before CONFIRM (target in sensor range/FOV).
- Confirmation return-path (7.1.7–7.1.10) routes to **R08 notification strip + audio ping** — shared, not new.

**S-17.1.2 — Contact-list selector panel (serves Be-17.1.2, Be-17.1.3).**
- Docked WAD panel listing catalogued/detected contacts (ID, bearing, range), navigable by **bezel rotary/OSS stepping** and selectable; **UCP alphanumeric** entry for direct ID or lat/long coordinate.
- Selected contact highlights its map marker (cross-links to S-17.1.1) — this is the Mixed handoff surface.
- Same TRACK TOI confirm gate as S-17.1.1 (shared).

**S-17.1.3 — Unified TOI panel (combines both above).**
- Single overlay with the map-designation surface and the contact list side-by-side in one panel state, sharing one TRACK TOI confirm control. Pilot picks spatially or from list interchangeably; one panel, one confirm.
- Trades screen real estate for a single coherent tasking surface.

Recommendation: **S-17.1.3** — it natively realizes all three behaviours in one place and makes the Mixed pathway (the realistic clustered-target case) frictionless, rather than forcing a mental switch between two separate structures. S-17.1.1 + S-17.1.2 as separate panels is the fallback if WAD space is contested.

Which structure?

**S-17.1.3 — Unified TOI panel** is closed.

**R17 final — all three layers:**
- **Function:** F-17.1 — Target designation-to-track function (convert a pilot-identified TOI into a validated track command to the UAV).
- **Behaviours:** Be-17.1.1 (Touch-only), Be-17.1.2 (Keyboard-only), Be-17.1.3 (Mixed) — all retained.
- **Structure:** S-17.1.3 — Unified TOI panel: single WAD overlay combining a map/feed designation surface (reusing R14's designation primitive, distinct target-reticle marker) and a bezel/UCP-navigable contact list, sharing one TRACK TOI dual-input confirm gate (R09/R10 lineage) with pre-confirm trackability validation; confirmation return-path routed through R08's notification strip + audio.

**Shared/reused flags for consolidation:**
- Designation mechanism ← R14 (sensor aim-point) — same primitive, different marker semantics.
- Confirm gate ← R09/R10 dual-input press-and-confirm.
- Confirmation return-path ← R08 notification/audio.
- Map surface co-resident with R14/R16 panes.

R17 is complete. Confirm to close the requirement, or reopen any layer.
